lesson.title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)
lesson.description: Os conceitos apresentados sobre redes neurais serão implementados utilizando a API Keras de Python em conjunto com o Tensorflow. Após este encontro, os estudantes deverão ser capazes de implementar Redes Neurais de diversas configurações utilizando as ferramentas apresentadas.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Keras high-level neural networks API
before_phase4_candidates.description: Keras is a high-level API for building and training neural networks, available both as a standalone library and integrated into TensorFlow as tf.keras, offering a simple and intuitive interface.
coverage_criteria: Identify Keras as a high-level API for neural networks.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Using Kaggle Kernels for Keras without local installation
before_phase4_candidates.description: Kaggle Kernels provide a cloud-based Python environment with Keras pre-installed, allowing users to start building models immediately without any setup.

extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a single, practical piece of knowledge about a tool that enables immediate hands-on practice, easily checkable with a short question.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Normalizing grayscale image data for neural network input
before_phase4_candidates.description: Pixel values in grayscale images (originally 0–255) should be divided by 255 to normalize them to a [0,1] range, improving neural network training stability.
coverage_criteria: Explain why image pixel values are normalized to [0,1].
Identify the operation used (dividing by 255).

before_phase4_candidates.label: One‑hot encoding for categorical labels in Keras
before_phase4_candidates.description: Categorical labels must be converted to one-hot encoded vectors (e.g., using tf.keras.utils.to_categorical) so that the neural network output can be compared against a probability distribution.
coverage_criteria: Define one-hot encoding for classification labels.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Building a Sequential model with Dense layers
before_phase4_candidates.description: A neural network in Keras can be constructed as a Sequential model by stacking Dense layers with specified neuron counts and activation functions (e.g., relu for hidden layers, softmax for output).
coverage_criteria: Write code to create a Sequential model and add at least one Dense layer.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Compiling a Keras model with loss, optimizer, and metrics
before_phase4_candidates.description: Before training, a Keras model must be compiled by specifying the loss function (e.g., categorical_crossentropy), optimizer (e.g., rmsprop), and metrics (e.g., accuracy) to configure the learning process.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Training a Keras model with model.fit
before_phase4_candidates.description: The model.fit method trains the model on features and labels, controlled by epochs (number of passes over the data) and batch_size (samples per gradient update), and outputs loss and accuracy.

reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate presents the basic system prerequisites, a single factual unit.

reconciled_candidates.description: By default, TensorFlow maps nearly all GPU memory to a process to reduce memory fragmentation, often occupying more memory than needed and preventing other processes from using the GPU.

reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept covering the foundational default memory behavior that motivates the need for configuration.

reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept presenting the first method for controlling memory allocation: setting a fixed limit.

reconciled_candidates.label: Configuring Memory Growth in TensorFlow
reconciled_candidates.description: Enabling memory growth (tf.config.experimental.set_memory_growth) makes TensorFlow start with minimal memory and increase it as needed, but it does not release acquired memory even after load decreases.
coverage_criteria: Student can write the code snippet for memory growth and explain the trade-off of not releasing memory.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept presenting the second method for controlling memory: enabling dynamic growth with a documented caveat.

reconciled_candidates.label: Monitoring GPU Memory with nvidia-smi
reconciled_candidates.description: The nvidia-smi command displays real‑time GPU memory usage, which helps observe how TensorFlow allocates memory under different configurations.
coverage_criteria: Student can run nvidia-smi and interpret the memory usage output before and after loading a TensorFlow model.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept providing the basic command-line tool for directly verifying memory allocation settings.

reconciled_candidates.label: Profiling GPU Usage with Weight & Biases and TensorBoard

coverage_criteria: Student can describe the types of GPU metrics available in Weight & Biases and how they help in selecting an optimal memory limit.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept introducing advanced profiling tools that provide deeper analysis for memory optimization.
